how_to_query:
# 1. LIST — India country facet (294 reqs). Paginate offset 0,20,...,280.
#    NOTE: a browser User-Agent is REQUIRED on the DETAIL endpoint or it returns HTTP 406.
curl -s -X POST 'https://db.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/wday/cxs/db/DBWebsite/jobs' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"appliedFacets":{"Country":["c4f78be1a8f14da0ab49ce1162348a5e"]},"limit":20,"offset":0,"searchText":""}'

# 2. FACETS — discover Country/Location/JobCategory ids (India = c4f78be1a8f14da0ab49ce1162348a5e)
curl -s -X POST 'https://db.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/wday/cxs/db/DBWebsite/jobs' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"appliedFacets":{},"limit":1,"offset":0,"searchText":"India"}' | python -c "import json,sys;[print(f['facetParameter'],[(v['descriptor'],v['count']) for v in f['values']]) for f in json.load(sys.stdin)['facets']]"

# 3. DETAIL — full verbatim job description. Base is .../DBWebsite + externalPath
#    (externalPath ALREADY starts with /job/ — do NOT add another /job/, that yields HTTP 406/404)
UA='Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/128.0.0.0 Safari/537.36'
curl -s -H 'Accept: application/json' -H "User-Agent: $UA" \
  'https://db.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/wday/cxs/db/DBWebsite/job/Mumbai-Nirlon-Know-Pk-B4-B5/Lender-Finance-EU----Associate_R0452758'

# 4. Full-text search restricted to India (searches DESCRIPTION text, not just titles)
curl -s -X POST 'https://db.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/wday/cxs/db/DBWebsite/jobs' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"appliedFacets":{"Country":["c4f78be1a8f14da0ab49ce1162348a5e"]},"limit":20,"offset":0,"searchText":"Power BI"}'

# 5. STUDENT PROGRAMMES — NOT on Workday for India. The authoritative table of
#    application windows + eligibility is server-rendered HTML here:
curl -sL 'https://careers.db.com/students-graduates/your-application/' -H "User-Agent: $UA" -o appl.html
#    then parse the <table> rows (Location || Programme || Division || Application period || Eligibility)

limitations:
WHAT I COULD NOT GET, PLAINLY:

1. NO INDIA STUDENT-PROGRAMME REQS EXIST TO SCRAPE. DB India's Graduate Programme and Summer Internship are not published as applyable reqs anywhere — not on Workday, not on careers.db.com. I probed 11 plausible alternate Workday site names on the db tenant (DBGraduates, DBStudents, Students, Graduates, DBWebsiteGrad, DBCampus, Campus, DBEarlyCareers, EarlyCareers, db_grad, DBGraduate) and every one returned HTTP 404. The only Workday site is DBWebsite. The India programme information exists solely as a server-rendered table on careers.db.com/students-graduates/your-application/, which I did parse in full and have quoted verbatim. Consequence: there is no link to send him, no req ID, and no application form. The route is institutional (DJSCE placement cell) and I cannot verify from any public source whether DJSCE is one of DB's unnamed "partner campuses" — DB never publishes that list. That is the single biggest open question in this report and only a DB employee or the DJSCE placement cell can answer it.

2. "OPEN" vs "CLOSED" FOR INDIA CAMPUS HIRING IS INFERRED, NOT STATED. The careers site gives only month ranges ("between October and December", "between July and December"). It gives no year, no exact dates, and no status indicator. I am reading "October and December" as October-December 2026 because the table is headed "2027 Graduate Programme" with a July 2027 start, but DB does not say so explicitly. Do not treat "opens within days" as confirmed fact — treat it as the most probable reading of an ambiguous line.

3. THE APPRENTICE ELIGIBILITY GAP IS MY INFERENCE, NOT DB'S TEXT. R0357981 and R0441975 state only "This 12-month apprenticeship, under India's National Apprenticeship Training Scheme". Neither req states a graduation-year requirement anywhere in its 54,000 characters. My conclusion that he cannot join before ~June 2027 comes from how NATS works (it requires a completed degree), not from anything DB wrote. I did not verify this against the NATS portal. He should confirm directly rather than self-reject.

4. NO CLOSING DATES ON ANY WORKDAY REQ. The Workday detail payload exposes postedOn and startDate but no endDate for any of the 294 India reqs — every endDate field came back null. So for the lateral roles I can tell you how fresh a req is but not how long it stays open. "Posted 30+ Days Ago" is as precise as Workday gets past 30 days, so R0415916 (CFO Intern), R0423747 (Private Bank Strategy), R0420223 and R0432129 could be anywhere from 31 days to a year old, and some may be stale evergreen reqs rather than live vacancies.

5. I READ 44 OF 294 INDIA REQS IN FULL. I pulled the complete list of all 294 and filtered by title keyword plus a description-level full-text sweep on Power BI, Tableau, "SQL Python analytics", "0-2 years", "fresh graduate" and "business intelligence" to catch analytics roles whose titles hide them (that sweep is how I found Lender Finance EU and Corporate Banking Capital Strats, neither of which a title filter would surface). But I did not fetch all 294 descriptions. A role with an opaque title and no matching keyword could have been missed. The 250 unread reqs are concentrated in Technology (91 in the Technology job category), Sales Coverage (65) and Operations (38) — categories he has excluded anyway — which is why I stopped, but it is not zero risk.

6. THE APPRENTICE MEGA-REQ SPANS 20 SUB-ROLES UNDER ONE APPLICATION. R0357981 contains Roles 1 through 20 across Mumbai, Bangalore, Pune, Jaipur and New Delhi. I have listed the Mumbai sub-roles individually with their own verbatim qualifications, but they share ONE req ID and ONE apply button. I could not determine from the posting whether an applicant can express a preference for a specific sub-role or is simply pooled. Several sub-roles I did not list carry hard blockers worth knowing: Role 1 (Jaipur) states "German Language B1/B2 level is must for this role" and "Ability and willingness to work in night shift is a must".

7. DUPLICATE AND MISLEADING URL SLUGS. Several DB reqs have a display title that disagrees with their URL slug, because the slug preserves an earlier version of the posting. Concrete cases in this report: R0416180 displays as "BMAG – Analytics Analyst, AS" but its URL slug is "Vendor-Management-Senior-Analyst--AS"; R0435091 displays as "Strategic Equity Transactions Group (SETG), EMEA (IBCM), AS" with slug "Origination-Enabler--AS"; R0437958 displays as "Risk Data Validation & Control, Associate" with slug "CRM---Relationship-Management"; R0448386 displays without a grade but its slug ends "--AVP"; R0439835 displays as "Data/Business Analyst, Credit Risk Change" with slug "Business-Analyst-AI-Translator--Credit-Risk--AVP"; R0424510 displays as "Market Risk Data Governance - Associate" with slug "Risk-Specialist--AS". The URLs I have given all resolve, but the displayed seniority can understate the real grade — in at least four cases the slug reveals an AVP-level role that the title hides.

8. API QUIRKS THAT WILL BITE ON A RERUN. The detail endpoint returns HTTP 406 without a browser User-Agent, and the list endpoint does not. Also, externalPath from the list response already begins with /job/, so the correct detail URL is .../DBWebsite + externalPath; concatenating .../DBWebsite/job + externalPath produces /job/job/ and a silent failure. Both are baked into the how_to_query commands.

9. NOT VERIFIED: SINGAPORE/HONG KONG VISA REALITY. I confirmed he meets every written eligibility line for the DWS P.A.C.E. programme and the 1 Sep - 11 Oct 2026 APAC graduate windows. I did NOT verify whether DWS or DB sponsors a Singapore Employment Pass or Hong Kong visa for an Indian fresh graduate with no prior work authorisation there, which is the actual determinant of whether those applications go anywhere. The eligibility text's silence on work authorisation is not the same as permission — note both Singapore and Hong Kong graduate reqs carry the phrase "subject to local working legislation and visa requirements" in the careers.db.com table.

10. SALARY, COHORT SIZE AND HISTORICAL DJSCE OUTCOMES: no data found. DB publishes none of it and I did not rely on third-party aggregator claims.
